subject: Support tiering, incident-credit matrix and escalation hours — proposal
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Walsh <emma@hearthanalytics.com>, Daniel Smith <daniel.smith@hearthanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@hearthanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:13:00 +0000
Subject: Support tiering + incident credit matrix — proposal

Hi Emma / Daniel,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attaching a proposed commit and incident-credit matrix so we have a concrete starting point for the SLA conversation. High-level options included:

- Tier A (Premium): 99.99% uptime, 24/7 on-call with 1-hour P1 response, credits scale from 5% — 50% of monthly commit depending on severity.
- Tier B (Business): 99.9% uptime, business-hours primary on-call with 4-hour P1 response, credits up to 20%.
- Tier C (Standard): 99.5% uptime, best-effort on-call, credits up to 10%.

Also included is an optional escalation retainer ($7k/mo) that guarantees a named escalation path and weekly on-call overlap during launches. The spreadsheet spells out exact credit triggers and calculation examples.

Questions for you:
1) Which uptime tier aligns with your regulatory/availability needs?
2) Any hard constraints on monthly budget we should consider for discounts/commit sizing?
3) Do you require 24/7 escalation coverage for P1s, or would a retainer be acceptable to extend guaranteed hours?

Next steps: if you can confirm the tier and preferred commitment length (12 / 24 / 36 months), we’ll produce a redline-ready SLA addendum and DocuSign envelope.

Attachments: proposed-commit-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform.
From: Emma Walsh <emma@hearthanalytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@hearthanalytics.com, Daniel Smith <daniel.smith@hearthanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Support tiering + incident credit matrix — proposal

Vivek —

Thanks for the detailed matrix, this is exactly what we needed to start procurement. A few quick notes from our side:

- Our preferred target is something equivalent to your Tier B (Business), but we have a constrained budget for H1 FY28 and would need a concession on list pricing to get to a deal this quarter.
- For mission-critical workloads we run across customer-facing products; we do need guaranteed 24/7 P1 acknowledgement. If that requires the retainer, we want to understand the effective blended price (commit + retainer).
- On credits: we prefer a simpler schedule (e.g., credits only if availability < 99.5% and stepping at 99% / 98%). We’ve found very granular bands are hard to reconcile during outages.

Action items from our side: please send a counter that includes a 12-month and 24-month commit option and the bundled price including the escalation retainer. Also please include SOC 2 evidence and point us to the DocuSign link when ready.

Thanks,
Emma
VP of Platform Operations, Hearth Analytics
emma@hearthanalytics.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Support tiering + incident credit matrix — proposal

Vivek —

Thanks for the context. Based on margin targets and the strategic nature of Hearth, here is a commercial counter we can present:

Option 1 — 12 months
- Commitment: 120k monthly equivalent (token-based pricing converted to an MRR for the term)
- Discount: 15% off list for Tier B (applies to compute token price)
- Escalation retainer: optional $7k/month — includes guaranteed named escalation and weekend overlap for launches
- Credits: simplify to three bands: <99.5% = 10% credit, <99% = 25% credit, <98% = 50% credit (credit calculated on monthly committed spend only)

Option 2 — 24 months
- Commitment: same monthly run-rate, 20% discount off list
- Escalation retainer: optional $6k/month (volume concession)
- Credits: as Option 1

Notes / negotiation levers:
- We can make the retainer mandatory for 24/7 acknowledgement if Hearth prefers that guarantee; otherwise we can define an SLA acknowledgement window backed by an on-call rotation (4-hour P1 acknowledgement outside business hours).
- Legal will prepare an SLA addendum. I’ll attach the proposed commit matrix to the reply.

Attachment: proposed-commit-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

If that framing looks okay I recommend we send the 24-mo option first (most attractive price) and include the 12-mo as fallback.

Laura Bennett
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Support tiering + incident credit matrix — technical note

Quick technical note to add to the commercial:

- Definitions: we should define P1 (service down: complete inability to serve inference requests for production traffic), P2 (degraded latency or partial feature outage), P3 (minor impact). The SLA measurement will be based on our ingestion of customer-side latency and successful token ingress/egress; this needs to be instrumented and mutually agreed.
- 24/7 acknowledgement: to guarantee immediate acknowledgement we need the escalation retainer so we can staff a primary responder within 60–90 minutes 24/7; otherwise the on-call rotation gives a 4-hour acknowledgement window off-hours.
- Remediation targets: propose 4-hour remediation target for P1 (work to restore partial service), 24-hour for P2. Credits kick only if remediation exceeds the target and uptime falls below the band.
- Operational tooling: we’ll enable shared incident channel (Slack + PagerDuty) and grant Hearth read-only visibility into incident timelines.

Attaching a short map of our escalation playbook and on-call overlap recommendations.

Attachment: redwood-escalation-map.pdf (PDF stub)

—Karthik
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Final — support pricing, incident credits, and next steps

Emma / Daniel / Procurement,

Appreciate the speedy back-and-forth. To summarize the commercial we’re prepared to present today:

Agreed target: Tier B (Business) with a 24-month commitment (RWI-2027-HA-19).
Commercials (24-month):
- Commitment: monthly equivalent as discussed
- Discount: 20% off list for Tier B pricing
- Escalation retainer: optional at $6k/month (includes named escalation and weekend overlap for launches). If Hearth requires guaranteed 24/7 P1 acknowledgement without the retainer, we cannot promise stricter than a 4-hour off-hours acknowledgement.
- Credits: simplified bands — <99.5% = 10% credit; <99% = 25%; <98% = 50% (credits applied to committed monthly spend).

Operational / technical items:
- Remediation targets: 4 hours (P1 partial restore), 24 hours (P2). Credits only apply when remediation windows are exceeded and the monthly uptime falls below the bands.
- Incident visibility: we’ll create a shared Slack channel and configure PagerDuty access for Hearth (read-only incident timeline).

Compliance & paperwork:
- SOC 2 report: https://redwood-inference.com/security/soc2 (link to report)
- DocuSign SLA addendum: https://www.docusign.net/envelope/RWI-HA-2027-19872 (envelope prepared)

Attachments delivered with this email: proposed-commit-matrix.xlsx, redwood-escalation-map.pdf, SLA-term-sheet-3.1.docx

Next steps:
1) Hearth to confirm acceptance of 24-mo commercial above (or request 12-mo option).
2) Procurement to review DocuSign envelope and return any legal redlines.
3) Upon signature, onboarding will schedule an incident runbook workshop with Karthik and the Hearth platform team.

If you want I can also prepare a blended price sheet that includes the retainer in the monthly equivalent (makes the procurement review easier).

Thanks and happy to jump on a 30m call if you prefer to finish this out quickly.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
